chunks: Hammād ibn ʿĪsā narrated from al--Ḥusayn ibn al-Mukhtār, from al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Kāmil who said:

Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) said: 'When you mingle with people, if you are able to ensure that your hand is uppermost over any one of the people you mingle with, then do so. Verily, the servant may have some shortcomings in his worship, yet he possesses good character, so Allah elevates him by his character to the rank of the fasting one who stands [in night prayer].'

key_terms.الصَّائِمِ الْقَائِمِ: The fasting one who stands (in prayer)
key_terms.يَدُكَ عَلَيْهِ عُلْيَا: Your hand is uppermost over him (having precedence/excellence)

ai.seo_question: How does good character compensate for shortcomings in worship according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Kitab al-Zuhd*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) highlights the compensatory power of noble character (akhlaq), explaining that it can elevate a believer to the spiritual station of 'al-sa'im al-qaim' (the fasting one who stands in night prayer) despite shortcomings in ritual acts. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the integration of inner piety with social conduct, where ethical excellence serves as a means of spiritual elevation and divine acceptance.
